title: Dont Take a Breath in a Brainstorm
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that effective brainstorming depends on maintaining an uninterrupted, judgment-free pace, and that leaders undermine their own sessions by pausing to evaluate ideas as they come in. The author describes the mechanics of a good brainstorm and contrasts it with the more common instinct to default straight to expert opinion. The piece speculates that leaders avoid brainstorming because it feels 'hokey' and pushes back directly against that instinct. It closes by noting that a full session can be run in well under 30 minutes.
points: Judging or commenting on ideas mid-brainstorm is described as the single biggest way leaders sabotage their own sessions.
Good brainstorming has a specific mechanic: pose the question, capture every idea without evaluation, and let one idea spark the next.
Leaders often default to expert opinion instead of group brainstorming because they perceive the exercise as insufficiently serious.
A full brainstorming session can be run in under 30 minutes, undercutting the excuse that it's too time-consuming.
quotes: The best brainstorming doesn’t stop or wait for commentary or evaluation. It moves at a furious pace.
Judging or commenting on ideas as they are shared puts a wrench in the gears of ideation.
In a true brainstorm, no idea is considered bad, stupid, or ridiculous. The only way to get others to think outside of the box is to avoid any judgment about anything that gets said.
The magic of brainstorming happens when one idea sparks another. Team members often expand and build upon earlier ideas no matter how crazy they may be.
Better yet, most sessions can be conducted in less than 30 minutes. Creativity is contagious. Brainstorming will show you how.
